approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules and describes them with count fingerprints. It fits the original count Gaussian process for dependence, while a frozen TabICLv2 model conditions on the same accepted scores to predict each candidate's quantiles. The tabular preprocessing drops columns that are constant in the accepted archive, then applies native normalization and eight feature views. Integrated quantile means set the inherited stall-dependent eligibility mask, and the original correlated Gaussian draws are transported through those quantiles to choose each paid batch. Accepted scores then update the archive, survivors and breeding state.
approach.novelty: Add one visibility adapter for count coordinates that are constant in the accepted archive but differ in fresh molecules. Keep the Parent's exact transforms for variable coordinates, represent each archive-constant coordinate as its raw count minus its accepted constant with unit scale, and restore original coordinate order before the same eight-view quantile model. This gives previously deleted query variation a route into predictions without inventing labels. There are no completed same-Parent siblings in the frozen brief; the concurrently scheduled sibling instead changes marginal location while retaining deletion. The historical full-coordinate TabPFN mean recipe used a different model and failed to improve ordering, so useful visibility here remains a testable claim.

observed_bottleneck: Code Parent n-16b934239c55 deletes archive-constant count coordinates before native prediction. Across all435 recorded batches and15 Search cells only296..1318 of2048 coordinates survive, and200..762 deleted coordinates differ in every fresh pool (mean399.64827586206894). This is an observed information boundary, not proof that it caused the loss. Native inference executed without recorded model failure or fallback, yet same-paid strict-pair accuracy was13209/19450=0.6791259640102828 versus13776/19450=0.7082776349614396 for original-GP means. Conditional pinball improved (0.013671119439650692 versus0.01493098618133278), while endpoint mean0.47377281306454333 (seed population SD0.03865070499495466) was0.13325750314658766 below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de, with all three seed deltas negative. Historical n-5277bf3b7425 exposed all2048 inputs to a different TabPFN mean recipe yet weakened ordering0.6571838638577067 versus0.6982418371008252; this limits transfer claims without deciding this adapter. New per-cell audits and every underlying run/summary/task-log/trajectory citation and hash are indexed together in policy/scratch/r0063-02-improve-L01/plan/evidence-index-refreshed.json; the complete derived aggregate is policy/scratch/r0063-02-improve-L01/plan/aggregate.json. The index lists all15 sanctioned per-cell audit files individually alongside their exact input files. The new audit replay verifies chronological contexts, purchased identity/score joins, exact defined-quantile moment arithmetic and ordering; it does not claim independent raw-feature reconstruction.

adoptions.applicability: The code Parent actually executed this fixed model on all435 pools. The paper does not establish molecular distribution-shift calibration or endpoint gain, and the Parent's paid ordering was refuted. Only inference capability is inherited.
adoptions.borrowed_element: The inherited fixed TabICLv2 regression model performs accepted-context native quantile prediction with its native target handling and eight feature views.

deviations.paper_setting: General tabular prediction with synthetic-pretrained model; distribution shifts and non-toy distributional validation remain limitations.
deviations.reason: Retain the already implemented Parent law while testing a measured representation obstacle; no source benchmark gain or calibration claim is transferred.

Native near-zero scaling and power/outlier transforms cannot be naively applied to those constant columns. The adapter is justified as a testable information exposure, not as a source-backed predictor improvement.

deviations.reason: The frozen continuation specifically tests the measured deletion boundary while avoiding synthetic labels, jitter and amplified near-zero-variance scaling. Query-only variation has no accepted label support and can be harmful or inert.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the exact frozen Search Policy review and its recorded queries; no fresh search is claimed. Adopt the existing native inference and explicit preprocessing boundary as the basis for one substantive visibility-adapter variant. All new evidence is from the frozen Search panel and supports a measurable obstacle, not presumed benefit. The complete Parent and historical full-coordinate TabPFN counterexamples remain valid. No checkpoint, model purpose, package, target-location substitution or additional intervention is introduced. Source inspection supports a concrete construction path, while actual2048-column/eight-view synthetic inference, numerical parity and bounded-resource feasibility remain mandatory and unmeasured until bound APPLY.

hypothesis: Modify only the representation delivered to the inherited native quantile/copula recipe. At every accepted-archive refit let V be the exact nonconstant columns of the original2048 float32 count matrix and C its complement. For each none/power normalization group, fit and apply the Parent's exact native PreprocessingPipeline to X[:,V]. Set each C-channel to X_j-c_j with c_j the common accepted raw count and unit scale; training values are exactly zero and unseen query differences remain raw unit-count differences. Reassemble columns in original0..2047 order, then use the unchanged session-seeded Latin shuffler, eight-view source model, native target pipeline,999-quantile grid, crossing/tail law, integrated moments and original-GP Gaussian-copula consumer. This changes the information visible at the observed deletion boundary. It does not assert that an unlabeled variation channel is predictive or that the Parent's refuted native-marginal ordering benefit is an inherited capability.

finding_summary.headline: Exposed count coordinates changed purchases but worsened paid ranking; endpoints improved only over the weaker Parent
finding_summary.insights:
The deletion boundary was real and the added signals reached both inference and subsequent search. Of the 1,626 different paid identities, all 1,582 with a following fit entered it, 1,319 were admitted as survivors, and 891 later generated pooled descendants. Missing exposure or a disconnected feedback path therefore cannot explain the ranking loss. The literature-derived native inference and preprocessing separation operated as implemented; the campaign-specific unit-count extension did not establish the useful-visibility prediction. Keeping query-only variation visible supplies no accepted labels for that variation, and the full-width view layout also changes model behavior; this experiment identifies a poor joint ranking intervention, not which of those two effects caused it. A ranking model that learns useful molecular comparisons, rather than visibility alone, is the relevant method-level distinction left open.

The endpoint gain does not rescue that prediction: almost all of the net Parent-relative gain comes from the docking task, while late incumbent increment mass falls from 1.763311 to 0.803828 across the panel. That mass telescopes to endpoints and is not independent corroboration. The molecular assessment shows broad graph variation contracting to only 2–11 typed scaffolds among each task’s highest thirty proposals; repeated large scaffold joins, unusual local bonds and unresolved stereochemistry remain. A proposal scheme with alternative ring and linker topology and conventional attachment environments could address that measured search limitation, but these trajectories do not establish its score benefit. The result settles this adapter’s registered ranking hypothesis, leaves its favorable total endpoint association separate from the unproven ranking explanation, and does not settle the wider approach.
finding_summary.results: All 435 pools exposed 225–762 previously discarded varying coordinates without changing native variable-column transforms. Zeroing only those new channels changed quantiles for 59,320 of 69,600 candidate rows and changed 204 paid sets; the complete adapter changed 428 of 435 sets against the filtered Parent, introducing 1,626 different paid identities. The registered prediction nevertheless failed: on the same 4,350 paid labels, strict-pair accuracy fell from 12,972/19,417 = 0.668074 to 12,567/19,417 = 0.647216 (-0.020858); 14 of 15 task/seed cells worsened. Late-half accuracy fell from 0.694858 to 0.659276. Pinball loss was also slightly worse, 0.015602 versus 0.015524, although intervals widened and coverage increased. Every formal session completed without fallback. Final endpoint mean rose from 0.473773 to 0.532213, a paired gain of 0.058441 with all three seed averages positive, but remained 0.074817 below the formal Anchor and missed its required 0.609030 threshold. The Child seed population SD was 0.010186. Task-safety thresholds were not supplied, so no task-safety conclusion is available.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, often halogenated scaffolds; compact amine families coexist with oversized assemblies and unusual local bonds
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of the accepted Search chemistry of n-929b144c9731, compared descriptively with code Parent n-16b934239c55. The frozen comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; all Child and published Parent trajectories for Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 were read, with no missing paths or unmatched cells. Each task supplies 870 evaluated optimizer proposals, excluding repeated initial records. Every Child proposal contains ring-closure text; aromatic-text incidence ranges from 0.777 to 1.0. These are substituted aromatic heterocycles, carbonyl-rich nitrogen rings, cyclic amines, fluorinated unsaturated cages and linked multi-scaffold assemblies. Broad graph variation across tasks and seeds coexists with narrow high-score families. RDKit-derived descriptions distinguish real atom/ring counts from the digest string counters. The Child has 436 proposals containing N-halogen bonds, 260 O-halogen bonds and 87 peroxide bonds, versus 334, 75 and 396 in the Parent. There are 647 Child proposals with at least 60 heavy atoms versus 571 in the Parent, and none with at most 6 versus 1. These bins describe both size tails; they are not recommended size limits. All Child structures parse, but successful parsing does not establish stability, synthesis, binding or medicinal usefulness. No proposal has a formal charge or assigned tetrahedral center; 1941 have RDKit-recognized unassigned centers. Neutral amines are present, so the zero charge count is not absence of ionizable chemistry. Provenance and every underlying file are recorded in policy/scratch/r0063-02-improve-L01/molecular/input_manifest.json; full-stream and high/low-cohort descriptor comparisons are in policy/scratch/r0063-02-improve-L01/molecular/pooled_chemistry.json. High/low cohorts use only existing trajectory scores. The statements below are chemistry associations on these purchased molecules, not mechanism activation, component attribution or evidence for an unseen target pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact indole-like or related fused nitrogen heteroaromatics bearing an aryl amide/carbonyl, methyl or methoxy groups and halogenated substituents. The optimizer spans 9 to 55 heavy atoms, with median 25; the highest thirty span 24 to 26. The digest aromatic-text and halogen incidences are 0.9989 and 0.9425. Seed 1 leaders have N-fluorinated anilides and N-O-N or N-N appendages; seed 2 retains a more ordinary N-H indole carboxamide, although chloromethyl/fluoromethyl groups remain. The core chemistry is recognizable, but the frequent N-halogen and unusual nitrogen attachments make the output only questionably synthetically plausible. The Parent also concentrates near 25 heavy atoms, with a seed 0 quinoline-like aryl ketone and a seed 1 N-brominated amide.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 231 evaluated proposals and in 29 of the highest thirty; the high score does not demonstrate that these are stable medicinal compounds.
Halomethyl groups, N-N/N-O attachments and occasional oversized scaffold joins complicate synthetic plausibility.
missing_features: Well-represented alternative ordinary carbonyl/heteroaromatic connectivities in the high-score cohort: the output repeatedly elaborates a narrow fused core, although the paired Parent shows a different ordinary carbonyl arrangement can score in the same region.

Broader high-score coverage with conventional amide and ring-nitrogen substitution; such environments are possible in the shown molecules but are poorly represented among the pooled leaders. No unobserved target-specific motif can be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The large methoxy-rich scaffold join at seed 0 evaluation 27 has 55 heavy atoms and score 7.725428226485038e-37. The compact seed 1 N-fluoroamide at evaluation 218 scores 0.46092619585962435; its chloromethyl-to-bromomethyl analogue at 225 ties exactly. Thus compact aromatic/carbonyl organization is associated with the high-score region, and these peripheral halogen exchanges do not resolve that region. This is not a general preference for small molecules: the low cohort also contains a 9-heavy-atom structure. Code-Parent seed 0 reaches 0.4711064141789182 with an ordinary aryl ketone; the Child seed 2 N-H amide reaches 0.4145039882261785. N-halogenation is therefore not established as necessary. The thirty highest Child proposals contain only 2 typed Murcko scaffolds versus 6 in the Parent.

per_task.generated_character: Large, aromatic-rich assemblies of pyridyl/pyrimidinyl and phenyl rings, chromone-like carbonyl heterocycles, nitriles, ethers, esters and carbonyl-rich nitrogen rings. Some seeds make expanded heterocyclic linkers and long unsaturated alkyl substituents. The full stream spans 27 to 120 heavy atoms and 3 to 24 perceived rings, median 69 heavy atoms; all proposals have aromatic and ring-closure text. Seed 2 builds a very large repeatedly linked heteroaryl framework, whereas seed 1 uses a smaller but still substantial carbonyl-rich assembly. Such products require demanding multi-step synthesis; size, repetitive aromatic architecture and unusual heterocyclic attachments weaken drug-like character. The Parent full-stream median is 56 heavy atoms, and its highest thirty have median 44 versus Child 114.5: larger Child leaders are a real chemical shift, not missing ring access.
liabilities: Extensive aromatic repetition, numerous ring junctions and very large molecular size make solubility and synthesis concerns reasonable structural hypotheses, not measured failures.
Expanded heterocycles, N-O attachments and unusual small-ring/cumulated-unsaturation products occur in the full stream even though several leaders avoid those specific flags.
missing_features: Compact, nonrepetitive alternatives carrying the same broad heteroaryl and carbonyl functionality are underrepresented among the Child leaders; all highest thirty have at least 60 heavy atoms, although the paired Parent demonstrates a smaller high-score family.

Simple linker and ring-connectivity alternatives that preserve productive aromatic organization without repeatedly appending entire scaffolds are not well represented in the upper Child cohort; the exact required connectivity cannot be identified from these scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The partially dearomatized seed 2 evaluation 16 structure scores 0.528153827722535. Seed 1 evaluation 291, with 60 heavy atoms, scores 0.6125834949364362; the huge seed 2 evaluation 284 structure scores 0.6119360365505425. The Child sampled gradient associates elaborate aromatic/heteroaromatic assemblies with the upper region, but even the much larger seed 2 assembly does not exceed the 60-heavy-atom example. The Parent seed 1 reaches 0.6338235294117647 with 48 heavy atoms, while its seed 0 leader is larger. Thus the paired chemistry does not establish a universal benefit from enlargement or aromatic repetition. The Parent leader also contains cumulated unsaturation, so it is not an unqualified synthetic-quality reference.

per_task.generated_character: Halogenated aryl groups coupled to cyclic amines and carbonyl or sulfur-containing linkers dominate. The stream spans 13 to 119 heavy atoms, median 35; the highest thirty span 28 to 33. Seed 0 leaders combine a halogenated anisole, a benzocyclobutene-like fused unit, an amino-ketone linker, pyrrolidine and an N-methylaziridine. Seed 1 instead shows a pyrrolidine-linked oxygen heterocycle and arylaminopyridine; seed 2 uses a bridged amine/sulfone framework. The highest thirty have 5 to 9 perceived rings and two aromatic six-membered rings each. Basic amine chemistry is already abundant. Ordinary aromatic and amino-ketone fragments coexist with strained ring junctions and unspecified configurations, so apparent synthetic plausibility is mixed. Parent leaders include a compact amino-rich aryl family, a bridged amine/sulfoxide cage and a sulfone/aminal family; the Child does not simply add previously absent nitrogen.
liabilities: Aziridine and fused four-membered-ring motifs in the highest-scoring seed 0 family raise ring-strain and reactivity concerns; they are structural flags, not measured instability.

Unspecified stereochemistry is pervasive, and other trajectories retain reactive halogenated sulfur/alkyl substituents or oversized joins. Neutral encoding does not specify the protonation state in a binding assay.
missing_features: Defined configurations for the multi-center high-score frameworks: all highest thirty have unassigned stereocenters and none has assigned tetrahedral configuration. These trajectories cannot establish which stereoisomers would preserve the score.

Broad representation of less strained, chemically conventional alternatives to the leading fused small-ring and aziridine connections. The seed 1 cyclic-amine family shows such alternatives are accessible, but no exact missing receptor-binding feature can be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The small fused N-sulfonyl seed 2 evaluation 74 structure scores 0.0016054506060786651. Seed 0 evaluation 283, with the integrated aryl/cyclic-amine/amino-ketone framework, scores 0.9932424000166679. Duplicating substantial amino-ketone/cyclic-amine functionality in seed 0 evaluation 300 enlarges it to 42 heavy atoms and scores only 0.07726651083830485. The observed contrast favors a particular connected presentation of hydrophobic rings and amines rather than nitrogen presence or molecular growth alone. Parent seed leaders score 0.7406513372419333, 0.9767993639759021 and 0.311587596471083; the chemical changes differ by seed and are not a matched binding-mechanism experiment.

per_task.generated_character: Aromatic, carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles evolve toward phenyl/alkoxy-substituted medium rings and fused or bridged cyclic amine/lactam systems. Seed 2 adds a benzofused cyclic O-CH2-O-carbonyl arrangement, a phenyl group, alkyl/ethoxy substituents and N-methyl groups around a compact fused nitrogen framework. The stream spans 20 to 81 heavy atoms, median 34; the highest thirty span 33 to 37 with 4 to 5 perceived rings. All proposals have aromatic and ring-closure text, but only 0.1931 have halogen text. Large early bis-scaffold ester/anhydride-like joins contrast with more compact later structures. These molecules have recognizable carbonyl/amine chemistry but challenging ring closures and undefined configurations. The Parent leaders have similar size and aryl/alkoxy/N-methyl carbonyl-rich ring organization, with more flexible enlarged nitrogen rings in some seeds.
liabilities: Complex fused nitrogen rings and medium-ring closures have uncertain synthetic accessibility; score improvement does not establish makeability.
Early scaffold duplication and occasional anhydride, N-halogen and peroxide chemistry add liabilities beyond the ordinary carbonyl/amine motifs.
missing_features: More distinct high-score ring/linker families that retain the compact aryl/alkoxy/carbonyl organization: broad full-stream variation contracts to 10 typed and 6 generic scaffolds among the highest thirty.

Specified stereochemical alternatives for the fused and bridged products; 27 of the highest thirty have unassigned centers, so the apparently productive three-dimensional organization is not stereochemically resolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed 1 evaluation 23 multi-scaffold join has 81 heavy atoms and score 0.10920820821346902. The seed 2 evaluation 238 compact ring system has 35 heavy atoms and score 0.23885129132415045. The high-score region therefore associates with consolidation of aryl, ether and nitrogen/carbonyl functionality, not wholesale scaffold duplication. Seed 2 evaluations 250 and 254 replace a phenyl methyl with thiol yet tie at 0.23317314179720172, showing that these peripheral changes are not distinguished by the observed score. Parent per-seed leaders are chemically related but score 0.2225098886497406, 0.2133584675546675 and 0.22020415990760814. These are descriptive family comparisons; no new target-specific motif is identified.

per_task.generated_character: The stream moves from aromatic carbonyl-rich scaffold joins toward fluorinated, more unsaturated/aliphatic heterocycles and cages. It spans 9 to 60 heavy atoms, median 29; the highest thirty span 25 to 31. Seed 0 produces an N-N=CH2 appendage on a cyclic amino-ketone, linked through a fluorinated N-methyl aromatic five-membered ring to an unsaturated oxygen ring carrying O-F. Seed 2 instead makes densely fused/bridged N/O cages with imine, carbonyl, alkene, fluorinated carbon and sometimes N-F or N-S attachments. Seed 1 retains a different fused carbonyl-rich N/O system. Aromatic-text incidence is 0.777 overall, whereas the highest thirty contain much less aromatic content. Ordinary size alone masks substantial strain and local-bonding concerns. The Parent also makes cages and fluorinated carbonyl heterocycles, but its O-halogen incidence is much lower.
liabilities: There are 220 O-halogen and 119 N-halogen proposals in this task; O-F hypofluorite-like and N-F motifs need chemical scrutiny despite high recorded scores.
Dense small-ring fusion/bridging, imine/hydrazone-like appendages, N-S attachments, peroxides and undefined configurations make many candidates doubtful medicinal structures.
missing_features: Consistent access to conventional local bonding while retaining compact heteroatom/fluorinated architecture: the high-score cohort still contains 8 O-halogen-bearing and 8 N-halogen-bearing proposals, with possible overlap.
Stereochemically specified, less strained alternatives to the cage families. No trajectory demonstrates that an unseen named pharmacophore or particular configuration is the missing answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 2 evaluation 25, a 60-heavy-atom aromatic scaffold assembly, scores 5.993859735965082e-48. Seed 0 evaluation 271, a 27-heavy-atom O-F-containing structure, scores 0.4661048425809384; replacing one aryl F with Br at evaluation 291 drops it to 0.08414870078169187. Seed 2 evaluation 221 with a hydroxymethyl group scores 0.42622417272758134; its otherwise matching hydroperoxymethyl counterpart at evaluation 300 scores 0.11086295220057707. These local contrasts support sensitivity to atom identity and oxygen placement, not a blanket reward for fluorination or reactive bonds. The Child sampled upper region favors compact, less aromatic heteroatom-rich structures. Parent leaders score 0.4746557230814677, 0.21976588771462166 and 0.524911241687462, with different scaffold families; neither expansion nor strain is established as necessary.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-929b144c9731, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2 and the complete evaluated proposal stream, 436 of 4350 proposals contain N-halogen bonds and 260 contain O-halogen bonds, compared with 334 and 75 in code Parent n-16b934239c55. Peroxide-bearing proposals fall from 396 to 87, so the liability pattern shifts rather than uniformly worsens. Some upper-score families retain N-F or O-F, while other upper-score families avoid them. These are RDKit bond flags in the authorized trajectories, not measured instability or component effects.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not reliably retain ordinary local bonding as productive scaffolds are elaborated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need reliable access to conventional attachment environments alongside its present scaffold edits, preserving useful ring/carbonyl arrangements while varying local bonding. A blanket chemical ban or score benefit is not justified by these associations; only current-session feedback can determine which alternatives matter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-929b144c9731 on the complete frozen Search panel, all 4350 evaluated proposals have zero charged atoms and zero assigned tetrahedral centers, while 1941 have at least one unassigned center. Cyclic amines, bridged frameworks and substituted small rings occur among the quoted upper-score structures. The same absence of assigned centers and formal charges is present in code Parent n-16b934239c55. Neutral representation is not absence of basic nitrogen, and no stereochemical or protonation benefit was measured.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks assigned tetrahedral configuration and explicit charge-state alternatives despite stereogenic and ionizable structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Chemically appropriate stereoisomer and ionization alternatives would expand representational coverage under the same canonical identity rules and task-local feedback. The required capability is expressing those alternatives; this evidence does not prescribe a configuration, charge, target interaction or intervention priority.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-929b144c9731 under the frozen Search panel, 647 of 4350 proposals have at least 60 heavy atoms versus 571 in code Parent n-16b934239c55; none has at most 6 versus 1. One upper-score family is dominated by very large aromatic assemblies, whereas other upper-score families are compact and their lowest-score examples include scaffold concatenations. A very large assembly and a substantially smaller assembly can occupy nearly the same score region. These are trajectory-conditioned size/connectivity associations, not a causal size law.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold elaboration does not consistently preserve access to compact, nonrepetitive alternatives alongside large ring assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to keep alternative linker lengths, scaffold joins and less repetitive connectivities available while retaining useful functionality. Both molecular-size tails must remain observable; this evidence supports neither a universal atom-count threshold nor a general preference for smaller molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the frozen Search panel for n-929b144c9731, full-stream typed scaffold counts range from 153 to 563 per objective, but the highest thirty contain only 2 to 11 typed scaffolds. Some leading families have strained fused small rings or aziridines; others have peripheral substitutions with exactly tied scores. In the entire Child stream 99 proposals contain a perceived aromatic ring of four or fewer atoms, versus 74 in code Parent n-16b934239c55. These are representation-level structural observations; scaffold counts do not identify which algorithm component caused them.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph variation does not consistently yield multiple chemically distinct high-score families with conventional ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Access to alternative ring topology and linker organization would complement peripheral substitutions, including less strained versions of useful motifs. Such coverage must remain task-agnostic and conditioned on the local observed scores; neither geometric flags nor scaffold diversity alone establish improved optimization.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
